major_concerns: Digital‑twin/emulator fidelity may not reflect production vendor idiosyncrasies (threat to external validity).
Engineering parity across verifier implementations is hard and may bias comparisons.
Prompt sensitivity and repair-loop design choices could drive results rather than verifier capability.
Potential lack of available vendor images for some multi‑vendor tests.
required_design_repairs: Pre-register a reduced, stratified intent set if full N=300 is infeasible; include power calculation for N.
Specify exact verifier implementations, versioned code, and engineering parity checklist.
Include prompt-sensitivity ablations and fixed prompt templates with seeds.
Declare emulator images, versions, and hashes and pre-validate key vendor behaviors; document known emulator limitations and their expected impact.

major_concerns: Risk of being judged a generic benchmark (track non-goal) unless scope emphasizes paired execution and operational-safety novelty.
Dataset curation bias toward emulatable topologies; vendor-image coverage gaps.
Reproducibility hinges on heavy artifact hosting and emulator version stability.
Five-page short paper may not allow full artifact description; risk of under-documentation.
required_design_repairs: Narrow to a compact, demonstrative corpus (e.g., 50–100 intents/topologies) for the paper and host full corpus externally with clear hashes and reproducible scripts.
Explicitly frame contribution as design+validation of paired-execution methodology with a small public proof-of-concept dataset rather than a full-scale benchmark release.
Pre-register selection criteria and emulator/image provenance; include reproducibility checklist and CI-friendly harness.
Plan artifact hosting (DOI/repository) and include emulator image hashes and exact versions.

major_concerns: Ethical risk of publishing exploit payloads and enabling reuse if not properly sanitized.
Emulation may not capture real supply-chain poisoning realism.
Defense implementations must be engineered fairly to avoid biased efficacy comparisons.
Defining exploit-success and acceptable false-positive tradeoffs requires careful preregistration.
required_design_repairs: Include responsible-disclosure policy and sanitize published payloads; publish only emulation-safe examples and detection rules.
Pre-register a precise threat model, exploit-success definition, and defense evaluation thresholds.
Ensure defense implementations parity checklist and versioned code release.
Report false-positive rates and time-to-detection; include sensitivity analyses for attack variants.

major_concerns: Scale and emulation resource demands (100–200 diverse topologies) may be infeasible within stated compute/time limits.
Incidence estimates will be conditional on emulator fidelity, vendor‑image coverage, and chosen LLM/prompt—risk of overgeneralization.
Predictor models risk confounding; observational association does not imply causation.
Reproducibility vulnerable to topology-generation stochasticity and emulator versions.
required_design_repairs: Reduce topology sample to a pre-registered, stratified subset with power justification; provide held-out validation topologies.
Pre-register topology-feature set and modeling pipeline; use simple, interpretable models as primary analysis and random-forest as secondary.
Specify and constrain compute/time budget; provide fallback plan (smaller sample) if emulation capacity is exceeded.
Report conditionality of incidence estimates (LLM, prompt, emulator) and avoid causal language; include sensitivity analyses.
